spike: SPIKE 5 — better-auth apiKey plugin: options, routes, hashing, lookup, permissions
claim: better-auth@1.7.5 ships an `apiKey` plugin with options `disableSessionForAPIKeys`, `enableMetadata`, `prefix`, `permissions`, rate limiting, `expiresIn`, and a server-side verify endpoint. `disableSessionForAPIKeys: true` is required to stop the plugin minting a mock session for a key (which would make an admin's API key grant full admin).
verdict: REFUTED — on the two things that matter operationally. (a) better-auth@1.7.5 does NOT ship the apiKey plugin at all; it was extracted to a separate package `@better-auth/api-key@1.7.5`, which is not installed. (b) The option `disableSessionForAPIKeys` does not exist. The real option is `enableSessionForAPIKeys`, with INVERTED polarity and a secure default of `false`. Everything else in the claim (enableMetadata, prefix, permissions, rate limiting, expiresIn, server-side verify) is CONFIRMED once the separate package is installed.

fallback_verified:
Yes, and it works. The fallback for "the plugin isn't in better-auth" is `npm install @better-auth/api-key@1.7.5` — the plugin was extracted to its own package, same version number, same maintainers (bekacru, better-gustavo), homepage still better-auth.com/docs/plugins/api-key. After installing, I stood up a real `betterAuth()` instance on `memoryAdapter` and exercised create / verify / list / update / delete, session-minting both ways, and the stored hash. All of it worked; no Postgres required. Cost of the fallback: one line in package.json and one changed import specifier, not 10-50 LOC.

The fallback for the option name is simply to not set anything: the secure behaviour (`enableSessionForAPIKeys: false`) is the default. I proved the wrong name is silently ignored rather than erroring — an instance configured `{ enableSessionForAPIKeys: true, disableSessionForAPIKeys: true }` still minted a full session for the key owner. So a spec that says "we set disableSessionForAPIKeys: true" would produce code that compiles, runs, and is wrong the moment anyone also enables the real flag.
impact:
Spec §14 needs four changes, none large, one of them a real design reversal.

1. DEPENDENCY (new): add `"@better-auth/api-key": "1.7.5"` and import `apiKey` from `@better-auth/api-key`, not `better-auth/plugins`. Any spec text, install list or import example saying otherwise will fail at `npm install` / first import. ~2 lines.

2. OPTION RENAME: `disableSessionForAPIKeys: true` -> `enableSessionForAPIKeys: false`. Polarity is inverted and the secure value is already the default, so the security posture the design wanted is what you get for free. Write it explicitly anyway as a tripwire. ~1 line.

3. METADATA DECISION REVERSES — this is the substantive one. The spec asks whether to put the MCP grant in `metadata`. Do NOT. With `enableMetadata: true`, the key's own owner can write arbitrary metadata through `POST /api/auth/api-key/create` AND `POST /api/auth/api-key/update` with nothing but their session cookie (verified: owner set `{role:"admin", tenant:"evil"}` and then updated it, both HTTP 200). `permissions` is guarded as SERVER_ONLY_PROPERTY and rejected 400 on both routes. Put every authorization grant in `permissions`; `metadata` is untrusted, owner-controlled input. Keep `enableMetadata: false`.

4. THE 404 LIST is 5 routes, not 6: create, get, list, update, delete. `/api/auth/api-key/verify` is not registered and already 404s — verification is server-only via `auth.api.verifyApiKey`. Blocking it is harmless but the spec should not imply it exists.

NOT changing: `prefix`, `expiresIn`, `permissions`, rate limiting and server-side verify all exist and work as the spec assumed. Key verification is a single indexed equality lookup (`findOne` on `apikey.key`, `index: true`), zero table scans — it is NOT mcphub's linear plaintext scan, so the replacement rationale holds. Keys are stored SHA-256 -> base64url-unpadded, never plaintext.
gotchas: The wrong option name fails SILENTLY. `disableSessionForAPIKeys` is not validated or rejected — an instance built with `{enableSessionForAPIKeys: true, disableSessionForAPIKeys: true}` still minted a full owner session. There is no runtime error to catch this; only the type checker would, and only if excess-property checking is in play.

`enableMetadata: false` (the default) rejects metadata even from a trusted SERVER-side `auth.api.createApiKey` call — 400 METADATA_DISABLED. So MCPRouter cannot use metadata for its own internal bookkeeping without also opening owner-writable metadata over HTTP. It's all-or-nothing. Another reason the grant belongs in `permissions`.

Rate limiting defaults to ON at 10 requests per DAY (`rateLimit: {enabled: true, timeWindow: 86400000, maxRequests: 10}`, index.mjs:2334-2338). A gateway that leaves this alone bricks every key on the 11th request. Set `rateLimit: {enabled: false}` or real numbers explicitly.

A failed PERMISSION check returns 401 KEY_NOT_FOUND, not 403 — and better-auth logs `ERROR [Better Auth]: Failed to validate API key` to stderr for it. Do not page on that log line, and do not infer 'key does not exist' from that code; it also means 'key lacks the permission'.
`verifyApiKey` returns `{valid: false, error}` instead of throwing. `if (await auth.api.verifyApiKey(...))` is always truthy — check `.valid`.
The owner column is `referenceId`, not `userId`. The create RESPONSE also carries `userId` in its OpenAPI schema, but the stored row and the DB index are `referenceId` (index.mjs:2146-2151).

`key` is declared `index: true`, NOT `unique: true`. The generated migration produces a plain index, so the DB will not stop a duplicate hash; uniqueness rests entirely on 64 chars of `generateRandomString(64, 'a-z','A-Z')`.

The `prefix` counts toward the key length and is stored in PLAINTEXT alongside `start` (the first 6 characters, also plaintext, prefix included). Useful for UI, but it means 6 characters of every key are recoverable from a DB dump.

`expiresIn` on create is in SECONDS, while `keyExpiration.defaultExpiresIn` in the plugin config is in MILLISECONDS, and `minExpiresIn`/`maxExpiresIn` are in DAYS. Three different units across one feature.

There is a stale doc comment at index.mjs:2464 claiming `POST /api-key/verify` is an endpoint. It is not registered — HTTP 404 with an empty body. Trusting the comment over the route table is exactly the kind of thing this spike existed to catch.

Anyone with a valid session can mint themselves a key via `POST /api/auth/api-key/create` by default (verified, HTTP 200). The design's 'mint only through our own POST /api/keys' is not the plugin's default — it requires actively blocking that route.
`betterAuth({database: fn})` accepts a raw adapter factory, which is how I wrapped the adapter to capture queries. Handy for asserting query shape in tests without a DB.
